title: Void vs voidable marriage - a distinction every client should understand
p1: A marriage can be called “invalid” and still have very different legal consequences. The difference between a void and a voidable marriage is one detail that can completely change a person’s rights and options.
p2: Many people assume both terms mean the marriage never existed. That is not always true. A void marriage is treated as invalid from the beginning, as if the law never recognized it. A voidable marriage, however, is considered valid unless one party takes legal steps to challenge and cancel it.
p3: This distinction matters in real life. Issues involving property, inheritance, children, and legal status can depend on whether a marriage was void or voidable. A surprising point many people miss: a voidable marriage does not disappear automatically — it usually requires a court process to set it aside. Knowing this difference early can prevent costly misunderstandings and wrong assumptions.
conclusion: Had you ever heard that a void and voidable marriage are legally different? What other legal terms do you think people commonly misunderstand?
